questions.q: How do most bats rest?
questions.fact: Bats have special tendons that lock their toes, so hanging takes no effort.

questions.q: Which animal is the slowest mammal in the world?
questions.fact: Sloths move so slowly that tiny algae grow in their fur, giving them a greenish tint.

questions.q: Which animal sleeps through winter in a deep, long sleep?
questions.fact: This long winter sleep is called hibernation.

questions.q: What is it called when an animal travels a long way each year to find food or warmth?
questions.fact: Some caribou herds migrate thousands of kilometers each year.

questions.q: What is it called when an animal's colors help it blend into its surroundings?
questions.fact: Arctic foxes turn white in winter and brown in summer to stay hidden.

questions.q: What do we call animals that are active mostly at night?
questions.fact: Owls, bats and raccoons are all nocturnal.

questions.q: What do we call an animal that eats both plants and meat?
questions.fact: Bears, pigs and most people are omnivores.

questions.q: What do we call an animal that eats only meat?
questions.fact: Cats are true carnivores and must eat meat to stay healthy.

questions.q: What do we call an animal that hunts other animals for food?
questions.fact: The animals that predators hunt are called prey.

questions.q: What do we call an animal that eats dead animals it did not kill?
questions.fact: Vultures are important scavengers that help clean up nature.

questions.q: What is a living thing that lives on or in another and harms it called?
questions.fact: Fleas, ticks and tapeworms are all parasites.

questions.q: What is the place where an animal naturally lives called?
questions.fact: A habitat gives an animal food, water, shelter and space.

questions.q: What do we call a type of animal that has completely died out?
questions.fact: Once an animal is extinct, it is gone forever.

questions.q: Which flightless bird from the island of Mauritius went extinct in the 1600s?
questions.fact: The phrase dead as a dodo comes from this bird.

questions.q: Which huge, hairy relative of elephants lived during the Ice Age?
questions.fact: Some woolly mammoths still lived on Wrangel Island until about 4,000 years ago, when the pyramids of Egypt already stood.

questions.q: Which bird, once the most common in North America, went extinct in 1914?
questions.fact: The last known passenger pigeon, named Martha, died at the Cincinnati Zoo.

questions.q: Which striped, meat-eating marsupial, also called the thylacine, went extinct in the 1900s?
questions.fact: The last known Tasmanian tiger, also called a thylacine, died in a zoo in 1936.

questions.q: Which dinosaur had three horns on its face and a big bony frill?
questions.fact: Triceratops means three-horned face.

questions.q: Which dinosaur had large plates along its back and spikes on its tail?
questions.fact: Stegosaurus had a brain about the size of a walnut, tiny for such a big body.

questions.q: Which famous meat-eating dinosaur had tiny arms and huge teeth?
questions.fact: A T. rex tooth, including the root, could be about 30 centimeters long.

questions.q: Which dinosaur had a club on the end of its tail and armor all over its back?
questions.fact: Ankylosaurus could swing its tail club hard enough to break bones.

questions.q: What were the flying reptiles that lived at the same time as dinosaurs called?
questions.fact: Pterosaurs were not dinosaurs, but they were close relatives.

questions.q: Which animals alive today are the living descendants of dinosaurs?
questions.fact: Scientists consider birds to be a group of small feathered dinosaurs that survived.

questions.q: What does the word dinosaur mean?
questions.fact: The name was made up in 1842 by scientist Richard Owen.

questions.q: Which long-necked dinosaur is one of the longest animals ever?
questions.fact: Argentinosaurus may have been around 30 meters long and weighed as much as several big trucks.

questions.q: What kind of animal is a seahorse?
questions.fact: Seahorses swim upright and steer with a tiny fin on their back.

questions.q: What kind of animal is a whale shark?
questions.fact: Even though it is huge, a whale shark eats tiny plankton.

questions.q: What kind of animal is a bat?
questions.fact: Bat mothers feed their babies milk, like all mammals.

questions.q: What kind of animal is a penguin?
questions.fact: Penguins have wings, but they use them like flippers to fly through water.

questions.q: What kind of animal is a salamander?
questions.fact: Salamanders look like lizards but have smooth, moist skin and no scales.

questions.q: What kind of animal is a jellyfish?
questions.fact: Jellyfish have been around for hundreds of millions of years, long before dinosaurs.

questions.q: Which feature do all mammals share?
questions.fact: Mammals also have hair or fur at some time in their lives, even whales.

questions.q: What are animals with backbones called?
questions.fact: Fish, amphibians, reptiles, birds and mammals are all vertebrates.

questions.q: What do we call animals that cannot control their own body temperature and depend on the outside?
questions.fact: Lizards bask in the sun to warm up before they get moving.

questions.q: Which group of animals includes snails, clams and octopuses?
questions.fact: Most mollusks have soft bodies, and many protect themselves with a shell.

questions.q: Which group of animals includes crabs, lobsters and shrimp?
questions.fact: Crustaceans have hard outer skeletons that they must shed to grow.

questions.q: Which animal can sleep for up to three years?
questions.fact: In very dry weather, some snails seal themselves in their shells and rest for a very long time.

questions.q: How does a snail move?
choices: By sliding on a muscle called a foot and a trail of slime
questions.fact: The slime helps snails glide over rough ground and even across sharp edges.

questions.q: Which small worm-like animal lives in soil and helps keep it healthy?
questions.fact: Earthworms have no lungs and breathe through their skin.

questions.q: Which animal has the most legs?
questions.fact: One millipede species has been found with more than 1,300 legs.

questions.q: Which animal has a stinger at the end of its tail and glows under ultraviolet light?
questions.fact: No one knows for sure why scorpions glow blue-green under UV light.

questions.q: What is a baby butterfly or moth called?
questions.fact: Some caterpillars grow to thousands of times their hatching weight.

questions.q: What is the only continent where no ants live naturally?
questions.fact: Ants live on every other continent, and there are thought to be quadrillions of them.

questions.q: Which animal is known as the ship of the desert?
questions.fact: Camels can go about a week or more without drinking water.

questions.q: What do camels store in their humps?
questions.fact: When a camel uses up its fat, its hump can get floppy and lean over.

questions.q: How many humps does a dromedary camel have?
questions.fact: Bactrian camels have two humps, and dromedaries have one.

questions.q: Which South American animal is related to the camel and often used to carry loads in the Andes?
questions.fact: Llamas may spit when they are annoyed, usually at other llamas.

questions.q: Which animal from the Himalayas has long shaggy hair and is used to carry loads at high altitudes?
questions.fact: Yaks have extra-large lungs and hearts to help them live where the air is thin.

questions.q: Which animal is the national animal of Scotland?
questions.fact: Scotland chose this mythical creature as a symbol of purity and power.

questions.q: Which animal lived on the Great Plains of North America in herds of millions?
questions.fact: Bison are the heaviest land animals in North America.

questions.q: Which is the largest kind of deer?
questions.fact: A big male moose can be over 2 meters tall at the shoulder.

questions.q: In which kind of deer do both males and females grow antlers?
questions.fact: Reindeer are called caribou in North America.

questions.q: What are antlers made of?
questions.fact: Most deer shed their antlers every year and grow new ones.

questions.q: What are horns on cattle, goats and sheep covered in?
questions.fact: Unlike antlers, true horns are not shed and keep growing.

questions.q: What is a rhinoceros horn made of?
questions.fact: Keratin is the same material as your hair and fingernails.

questions.q: Which animal has the thickest fur of any marine mammal?
questions.fact: A sea otter has about a million hairs in every square inch of skin.

questions.q: What color is a polar bear's skin?
questions.fact: Its fur hairs are actually clear and hollow, and they look white by reflecting light.

questions.q: What do polar bears mainly hunt?
questions.fact: Polar bears and penguins never meet in the wild because they live at opposite ends of Earth.

questions.q: Which bear is the largest meat-eating land mammal?
questions.fact: A big male polar bear can weigh more than 600 kilograms.

questions.q: Which bear is the smallest?
questions.fact: Sun bears have very long tongues for licking honey and insects out of trees.

questions.q: Which bear has a hump on its shoulders made of muscle?
questions.fact: The muscle hump helps grizzlies dig with their long claws.

questions.q: Where do wild giant pandas live?
questions.fact: Giant pandas live in cool, misty bamboo forests in the mountains of central China.

questions.q: What is special about a giant panda's wrist?
choices: It can spin in a circle
It has an extra bone that works like a thumb
questions.fact: The pseudo-thumb helps pandas grip bamboo stalks.

questions.q: Which African animal has black and white striped fur?
questions.fact: Each zebra has its own stripe pattern, like a fingerprint.

questions.q: Which animal looks like a mix of a zebra and a giraffe but is related to the giraffe?
questions.fact: The okapi lives in the rainforests of the Democratic Republic of the Congo.

questions.q: How long is a giraffe's tongue?
questions.fact: A giraffe's dark tongue may help protect it from sunburn while it eats.

questions.q: How many neck bones does a giraffe have?
questions.fact: Each giraffe neck bone can be more than 25 centimeters long.

questions.q: Which African animal spends its days in water and can be very dangerous?
questions.fact: Hippos cannot really swim, they walk or bounce along the river bottom.

questions.q: What does the name hippopotamus mean?
questions.fact: Hippos make their own reddish skin oil that may help protect them from the sun.

questions.q: Which animal is famous for curling into a spiky ball?
questions.fact: A hedgehog has about 5,000 to 7,000 spines.

questions.q: Which animal is covered in scales and is one of the most trafficked mammals in the world?
questions.fact: Pangolins roll into a tight ball of scales when frightened.

questions.q: Which animal eats ants and termites with a very long sticky tongue but has no teeth?
questions.fact: A giant anteater's tongue can flick in and out about 150 times a minute.

questions.q: Which animal's name comes from an Afrikaans word meaning earth pig?
questions.fact: Aardvarks dig burrows that many other animals later use as homes.

questions.q: Which small African mammal stands on its back legs to keep watch?
questions.fact: Meerkats take turns as sentries, calling out warnings when danger comes.

questions.q: Which animal is famous for being stubborn and is a relative of the horse?
questions.fact: Donkeys are actually careful, and they stop when they sense danger.

questions.q: What is a mule?
choices: The baby of a male donkey and a female horse
questions.fact: Mules are usually not able to have babies of their own.

questions.q: Which horse breed is often known as the fastest for short sprints?
questions.fact: Quarter horses got their name from racing a quarter mile.

questions.q: How do horses usually sleep?
choices: Often standing up, with special locking legs
questions.fact: Horses do need to lie down sometimes to get deep sleep.

questions.q: How do scientists measure a horse's height?
questions.fact: One hand equals 4 inches, about 10 centimeters.

questions.q: Which farm animal has a stomach with four parts?
questions.fact: Cows chew their cud, which is food brought back up to chew again.

questions.q: Which farm animal is known for being very smart and learning tricks quickly?
questions.fact: Pigs can learn their names and play simple video games with joysticks in experiments.

questions.q: Why do pigs roll in mud?
choices: To keep cool and protect their skin
questions.fact: Pigs have very few working sweat glands.

questions.q: Which bird lays the eggs that most people eat?
questions.fact: There are more chickens on Earth than any other bird.

questions.q: What is the fleshy red part on top of a chicken's head called?
questions.fact: The red flaps under the beak are called wattles.

questions.q: What is wool mostly from?
questions.fact: A sheep that is never sheared will keep growing more and more wool.

questions.q: Which pet animal is descended from wolves?
questions.fact: Dogs were tamed from wolves many thousands of years ago, long before farming began.

questions.q: Which dog breed is known as the fastest?
questions.fact: Greyhounds can reach about 70 kilometers per hour.

questions.q: Which dog breed was bred to hunt badgers and has a long body and short legs?
questions.fact: Dachshund means badger dog in German.

questions.q: Which is the smallest dog breed?
questions.fact: Chihuahuas are named after a state in Mexico.

questions.q: Which dog breed often works as a rescue dog in the Swiss Alps?
questions.fact: Saint Bernards are famous in stories for carrying small barrels, but that is mostly a myth.

questions.q: Which dog breed has spots and was once used to run beside horse-drawn fire carts?
questions.fact: Dalmatian puppies are born pure white and get their spots as they grow.

questions.q: Which dog breed is famous for pulling sleds in cold places?
questions.fact: Some huskies have one blue eye and one brown eye.

questions.q: How does a dog cool itself down?
questions.fact: Dogs only have a few sweat glands, mostly in their paw pads.

questions.q: How good is a dog's sense of smell compared to a person's?
questions.fact: Dogs can be trained to sniff out lost people, bombs and even some illnesses.

questions.q: Why do cats purr?
choices: Often when happy, but also to calm themselves
questions.fact: Cats may purr when they are hurt or scared too, which may help soothe them.

questions.q: What are a cat's whiskers mainly used for?
choices: Feeling their way and sensing things nearby
questions.fact: A cat's whiskers are usually about as wide as its body, helping it judge tight spaces.

questions.q: Which animal can see colors humans cannot, like ultraviolet light?
questions.fact: Many flowers have ultraviolet patterns that guide bees to their nectar.

questions.q: Which animal has the best color vision, with many types of color cells in its eyes?
questions.fact: Mantis shrimp have 12 to 16 kinds of color-sensing cells, while humans have 3.

questions.q: Which animal has the most powerful punch for its size?
questions.fact: A mantis shrimp's punch is fast enough to crack snail shells and even aquarium glass.

questions.q: Which animal is the loudest in the world?
questions.fact: A sperm whale's clicks are the loudest sounds made by any animal.

questions.q: Which animal is known for having a memory so good that it remembers watering holes for decades?
questions.fact: Older female elephants lead their herds to water using memories from many years before.

questions.q: Can goldfish really only remember things for three seconds?
choices: They have no memory at all
No, they can remember for months
questions.fact: Scientists have trained goldfish to respond to sounds and remember for months.

questions.q: Which animal has fingerprints almost like a human's?
questions.fact: Koala fingerprints are so similar to ours that they could be confused under a microscope.

questions.q: Which animal can survive being frozen solid in winter and thaw back to life in spring?
questions.fact: Wood frogs fill their cells with sugar, which works like antifreeze.

questions.q: Which tiny animal can survive outer space, boiling and freezing?
questions.fact: Tardigrades are also called water bears and are less than a millimeter long.

questions.q: Which jellyfish can turn back into a young form and start its life over?
questions.fact: Its scientific name is Turritopsis dohrnii.

questions.q: Which jellyfish is the longest, with tentacles that can reach over 30 meters?
questions.fact: That is longer than a blue whale.

questions.q: Which animal is the oldest known individual animal ever found?
questions.fact: A clam named Ming, found near Iceland, was about 507 years old.

questions.q: Which animal sleeps the most, about 20 hours a day?
questions.fact: Giraffes and elephants, on the other hand, sleep only a few hours a day.

questions.q: Which tall animal often sleeps standing up, in naps only minutes long?
questions.fact: Giraffes sleep only a few hours a day in total.

questions.q: Which animal's heart beats only a few times a minute when it dives deep?
questions.fact: A blue whale's heart has been measured beating as slowly as 2 times a minute during a dive.

questions.q: What is the name of the colorful flap of skin that helps a male frigatebird attract a mate?
questions.fact: The male puffs up his red throat pouch like a big balloon.

questions.q: Which long-legged bird wades in shallow water and spears fish with its sharp beak?
questions.fact: Herons stand very still, then strike quickly with their sharp beaks.

questions.q: Which large, flightless parrot from New Zealand is critically endangered?
questions.fact: Every living kakapo has a name and is watched closely by scientists.

questions.q: Which huge South American vulture is one of the largest flying birds in the world?
questions.fact: Andean condors can soar for hours without flapping their wings.

questions.q: Which bird is famous for laying its eggs in other birds' nests?
questions.fact: The other birds raise the cuckoo chick as if it were their own.

questions.q: Which bird can dive deeper than any other?
questions.fact: Emperor penguins can dive to more than 500 meters deep.

questions.q: Which bird has red feathers and is the state bird of seven US states?
questions.fact: Only male cardinals are bright red, and the females are a soft brown.

questions.q: Which bird is known for building mud nests and catching insects while flying low over fields?
questions.fact: Barn swallows often build their nests under bridges and inside barns.

questions.q: Which bird's name is also the name of a famous fast-running cartoon character?
questions.fact: Real roadrunners can run about 30 kilometers per hour and eat lizards and even snakes.

questions.q: Which bird did Benjamin Franklin praise as more respectable than the bald eagle?
questions.fact: He wrote this in a 1784 letter to his daughter, but he never officially proposed the turkey as the national bird.

questions.q: What color are a robin's eggs?
questions.fact: The color is so famous that robin egg blue is a color name.

questions.q: Which bird is the symbol of wisdom in many stories?
questions.fact: In ancient Greece, the owl was linked with Athena, the goddess of wisdom.

questions.q: How do birds that eat seeds grind their food without teeth?
choices: With a muscular stomach called a gizzard
They swallow seeds whole and never grind them
questions.fact: Many birds swallow tiny stones that help the gizzard grind food.

questions.q: Which animal has blue blood and has barely changed in hundreds of millions of years?
questions.fact: Horseshoe crab blood is used to test medicines for germs.

questions.q: Which animal can regrow its whole body from just a small piece?
questions.fact: Some flatworms called planarians can regrow a whole new body from a tiny piece.

questions.q: Which ocean animal has a body shaped like a disk and a long tail with a stinging spine?
questions.fact: Stingrays are close relatives of sharks and also have skeletons made of cartilage.

questions.q: Which is the largest ray, with fins that can stretch about 7 meters wide?
questions.fact: Manta rays have one of the biggest brains, for their size, of any fish.

questions.q: Which huge deep-sea animal was first photographed alive in the wild in 2004?
questions.fact: Japanese scientists took the photos almost 900 meters deep in the Pacific Ocean.

questions.q: Which sea creature has a spiral shell with many chambers and relatives that go back about 500 million years?
questions.fact: A nautilus moves up and down by changing the amount of gas in its shell chambers.

questions.q: Which spiny round sea animal is a favorite food of sea otters?
questions.fact: Sea urchins move slowly on hundreds of tiny tube feet.

questions.q: Which sea animal can throw out its insides to scare predators and then regrow them?
questions.fact: Some sea cucumbers shoot out sticky threads to tangle up attackers.

questions.q: Which ocean animal makes pearls?
questions.fact: A pearl forms when a mollusk coats a bit of grit or irritation with layers of shiny material.

questions.q: Which tiny ocean creatures are the main food of many whales, penguins and seals in the Southern Ocean?
questions.fact: Antarctic krill are among the most plentiful animals on Earth, with hundreds of trillions of them.

questions.q: What is plankton?
choices: Tiny living things that drift in water
questions.fact: Plankton made by tiny ocean plants produce a large share of the oxygen we breathe.

questions.q: Which fish can glide above the water for long distances using big fins like wings?
questions.fact: Flying fish can glide for about 200 meters by leaping out of the water.

questions.q: Which fish has a long, flat, sword-like bill?
questions.fact: Swordfish can heat their eyes and brains to see better in cold, deep water.

questions.q: Which fish is the heaviest bony fish in the world?
questions.fact: An ocean sunfish, also called a mola, can weigh more than 2,000 kilograms.

questions.q: Which fish can live out of water and even climb onto mangrove roots?
questions.fact: Mudskippers breathe through their skin and through water they hold in their gill chambers.

questions.q: What is a male deer called?
questions.fact: A female deer is called a doe.

questions.q: What is a male sheep called?
questions.fact: A female sheep is called a ewe.

questions.q: What is a female horse called?
questions.fact: An adult male horse is called a stallion.

questions.q: What is a male chicken called?
questions.fact: Roosters crow at many times of the day, not only at sunrise.

questions.q: What is a female pig called?
questions.fact: A male pig is called a boar.

questions.q: What is a male duck called?
questions.fact: Many male ducks have bright colors, while females are brown to stay hidden on the nest.

questions.q: What is a male goose called?
questions.fact: A female goose is simply called a goose.

questions.q: Which type of animal is the axolotl, which is often called a Mexican walking fish?
questions.fact: Axolotls usually keep their feathery gills and live in water their whole lives.

questions.q: Which animal can jump the highest compared to its body size?
questions.fact: A flea can jump more than 100 times its own body length.

questions.q: How far can a red kangaroo jump in a single hop?
questions.fact: Kangaroos cannot easily walk backward.

questions.q: What does a kangaroo use its strong tail for?
choices: Balance and support, like a fifth leg
questions.fact: When moving slowly, a kangaroo leans on its tail while it swings its legs forward.

questions.q: Which animal has a nose like a short trunk and lives in rainforests of South America and Asia?
questions.fact: Baby tapirs have stripes and spots that fade as they grow.

questions.q: Which cat has a very short tail and tufted ears and lives in northern forests?
questions.fact: Lynx have huge, furry paws that work like snowshoes.

questions.q: Which wild cat of the Americas is also called a cougar, puma or mountain lion?
questions.fact: It holds the record for the animal with the most common names in English.

questions.q: Which small wild cat of North America is named for its short tail?
questions.fact: Bobcats are about twice the size of a pet cat.

questions.q: Which wild African cat has very long legs and big ears to hear prey in tall grass?
questions.fact: Servals can leap high into the air to catch birds.

questions.q: Which weasel relative is famous for being fearless and fighting much bigger animals?
questions.fact: Honey badgers have thick, loose skin that makes them hard to grab.

questions.q: Which animal is famous for washing its food in water before eating?
questions.fact: Raccoons are actually feeling their food, since wet paws are extra sensitive.

questions.q: Which animal is red, fluffy and lives in the Himalayas, though it is not a bear?
questions.fact: Red pandas were named pandas before giant pandas were.

questions.q: Which fox lives in the Sahara Desert and has huge ears?
questions.fact: Its big ears help it hear prey underground and also give off heat to stay cool.

questions.q: Which tiny primate has eyes so big that each one is about as large as its brain?
questions.fact: Tarsiers cannot move their eyes, so they turn their heads instead, like owls.

questions.q: Which wild pig of Africa has warts on its face?
questions.fact: Warthogs kneel on their front knees when they eat grass.

questions.q: Which antelope can leap about 3 meters high and is common in African savannas?
questions.fact: When running from danger, impalas leap in many directions to confuse predators.

questions.q: Which large animal of Africa travels with zebras in a giant migration each year?
questions.fact: More than a million wildebeest travel across the Serengeti and Masai Mara each year.

questions.q: Which animal has the thickest skin of any land mammal?
questions.fact: Rhino skin can be about 5 centimeters thick in places.

questions.q: Which rhinoceros is the largest kind?
questions.fact: Both white and black rhinos are actually gray.

questions.q: Which animal is the national animal of Australia, along with the emu?
questions.fact: The kangaroo and emu both appear on Australia's coat of arms.

questions.q: Which animal is the national animal of China?
questions.fact: Giant pandas have been sent to zoos in other countries as signs of friendship.

questions.q: Which animal on the endangered list was saved partly because the United States banned the pesticide DDT?
questions.fact: DDT made eggshells so thin they broke before hatching.

questions.q: Which ape is critically endangered and lives in the mountains of Rwanda, Uganda and Congo?
questions.fact: As of 2025, there are only about 1,000 mountain gorillas, but their numbers have been slowly growing.

questions.q: What kind of fish is Nemo in the movie Finding Nemo?
questions.fact: All clownfish are born male, and some later change into females.

questions.q: Which cartoon character from Finding Nemo is a blue tang?
questions.fact: Blue tangs have sharp spines near their tails for defense.

questions.q: Which pet fish was first kept by people in ancient China?
questions.fact: Goldfish come from a wild carp and were bred in China over a thousand years ago.

questions.q: Which fish is also called the Siamese fighting fish?
questions.fact: Male bettas build nests out of bubbles on the water's surface.

questions.q: Which pet reptile is a popular lizard from Australia known for its spiky beard?
questions.fact: Bearded dragons puff out and darken their beards when they feel threatened.

questions.q: Which bird's heart can beat more than 1,000 times a minute?
questions.fact: Hummingbirds burn so much energy that they must feed many times every hour.

questions.q: Which group of animals has the most known species?
questions.fact: Scientists have named about a million insect species, and there are many more to find.

questions.q: Which insect is famous for its praying pose and for catching other insects with spiky front legs?
questions.fact: A praying mantis can turn its head almost all the way around to look behind it.

questions.q: Which insect makes a big ball-shaped paper nest from chewed wood?
questions.fact: Wasps were making paper long before people learned how.

questions.q: Which insect sense organ helps ants and moths smell?
questions.fact: Some male moths can smell a female from kilometers away with their feathery antennae.

questions.q: How many eyes do most spiders have?
questions.fact: Jumping spiders have two huge front eyes that give them sharp vision.
